summary: Specifies a new extension for Mobile IPv4 that the Home Agent and Foreign Agent can add to Registration Reply messages. It carries a text string meant for the user of the Mobile Node. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: When a traveling device checks in, the network can send back a short text message meant for a person. This note defines where that text goes.

questions: what is the mobile ipv4 message string extension
how to send text messages in mobile ip replies
what is mobile ip extension type 145
how does a home agent send a text message to a mobile node
what encoding does the mobile ip message string use
subtitle: A way for Mobile IPv4 agents to attach a human-readable text message to registration replies.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv4 registration results come back as reason codes, which tell the user of a Mobile Node very little about why a registration failed or succeeded.
tldr.mechanism: A new skippable extension, type 145, lets the Home Agent (sub-type 1) or Foreign Agent (sub-type 2) add a UTF-8 text string to registration messages sent to the Mobile Node.
tldr.outcome: The Mobile Node can show, log or otherwise handle the string, but the text MUST NOT affect protocol operation.

today: RFC 4917 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why a Message String
sections.content:
RFC 4917 defines a new skippable extension that a Foreign Agent or Home Agent can add to a registration message aimed at a Mobile Node. That message may be a Registration Reply or a Registration Revocation. On a Registration Reply the extension can be added whether the registration succeeded or failed.

The content of the string and what the Mobile Node does with it are implementation specific. It is meant for the user of the Mobile Node, so it can be displayed, logged or handled in some other way. Typical text gives a failure reason or a welcome message. The RFC says this matters because the failure reason code gives very limited information to a user, for example a string like "registration failed : Prepaid Quota for the user is exhausted".
sections.eli5: A number code like "error 3" does not help most people. A short sentence in plain words does.

sections.title: The Extension Format
sections.content:
The extension uses the Short Extension format from RFC 3344. It has a Type, a Length, a Sub-Type and then the Text.

  • Type: 145, an 8-bit identifier.
  • Length: an 8-bit unsigned integer giving the extension length in bytes, not counting the Type and Length fields. It MUST be 1 plus the total length of the Text field.
  • Sub-Type: 1 means the extension comes from the Home Agent, 2 means it comes from the Foreign Agent.
  • Text: one or more octets, implementation dependent, intended to be human readable, and it MUST NOT affect the operation of the protocol. It MUST be UTF-8 encoded ISO-10646 (RFC 3629).

The number of octets in the encoded text is always exactly Length minus one. The number of Unicode characters can be smaller than the number of octets.
sections.eli5: It is a small labeled box: a tag saying what kind of box it is, how big it is, who sent the note, and then the note itself written in a standard alphabet.

sections.title: How the Extension Is Used
sections.content:
The extension is valid only inside Mobile IPv4 Registration Reply and Registration Revocation messages. The Home Agent, the Foreign Agent or both may add it. The Mobile Node may throttle how often it notifies the user of the message.

The RFC gives an example. A Home Agent rejects a first Registration Request because the user's prepaid quota is reached, and attaches the text "Prepaid quota reached. Please contact www.paymore.example.com to update balance". The user tops up and retries. The Home Agent then accepts and attaches a welcome text, which confirms to the user that the binding was created.

If the Home Agent gets the message from elsewhere, such as a RADIUS server (RFC 2865), in another encoding, the Home Agent MUST convert it to UTF-8.
sections.eli5: If your account is out of credit, the network can say so in words. After you pay, it can say "welcome". Your phone decides how to show it, and will not nag you too often.

sections.title: Ordering and Protection
sections.content:
Protection of the extension depends on the ordering rules for message authentication in RFC 3344.

  • If added by the Home Agent (sub-type 1) to a Registration Reply or Registration Revocation, it MUST appear before the Mobile-Home Authentication Extension.
  • If added by the Foreign Agent (sub-type 2) to a Registration Reply, it MUST appear after the Mobile-Home Authentication Extension when that is present, and before the Mobile-Foreign Authentication Extension when that is present.

A security association between the Mobile Node and Foreign Agent is optional, so the Foreign Agent's extension may be unauthenticated. The extension gives no confidentiality: the message travels unencrypted, so sensitive information may need protection by other means.
sections.eli5: The note must sit in the right spot in the stack so the official stamp covers it. Some notes might not be stamped at all, and anyone could read them on the way.

sections.title: Number Assignments
sections.content:
The RFC reserves number 145 for the Message String Extension from the space of skippable mobility extensions, which is 128-255 and was defined for Mobile IPv4 in RFC 3344.

It also creates a new sub-type space for this extension type. Value 1 is reserved for use by the Home Agent and value 2 for the Foreign Agent. Future allocations from this space require expert review, following the procedures for the Mobile IPv4 number spaces.
sections.eli5: The RFC claims one number on the official list for this note type, and starts a small list of its own with two entries: one for each sender.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Extension length in bytes excluding Type and Length; 1 plus the Text length.

fields.name: Sub-Type
fields.desc: 1 for Home Agent, 2 for Foreign Agent.
